> Please add more details

What details are you looking for? It's a personal project, so I don't want to attach it.
Something about what kind of project causes this, any details at all on how to replicate this

I think I ran into the same problem.

- Linux Manjaro
- upgrading from 4.7.x (it's happening for 4.7.1 and 4.7.2 at the least)
- to 4.8-dev3

The strangest thing is that, even after doing a `git reset --hard`, removing the `.godot` folder, and removing all of the `*.import` files, it will then _also_ refuse to open in 4.7.x (well, _sometimes_ removing the import files works, but more often than not, it's a crash...).

I wanted to investigate a little bit further (like is it dev3 only? does it also happen for 4.7.0?), but the nature of restoring the project each time makes that time-intensive. I _did_ manage to find out that checking or unchecking the 'for all folders' option doesn't seem to make a difference though.

I'll try to attach the minimal reproduction project and the logs here

Steps to repro:
- Open project in 4.7.x; it should work properly.
- Open project in 4.8-dev3; it should ask to upgrade.
  - ... this crashes
- Now reset (via git or something -- though to save space I opted to not include the .git folder)
- Try top open again in 4.7.x
  - ... this _also_ crashes from now on

minimal (well, minimal _enough_ I think) reproduction project:
[upgrade_472_48dev3_.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31316048/upgrade_472_48dev3_.zip)

This crash, doesn't appear every time the project is upgraded but occurs offen enough to be reproducible.

When the project upgrades it appears that _connect_to_scene_recursive is being called multiple times for the
same node.  This includes the root node.

===== NEW ROOT TRAVERSAL 0x55c7b49c15d0 =====
....
CHILD ENTERED callback: child=0x55c7b026aa20 base=0x55c7b49c15d0
CALL _connect_to_scene_recursive: current=0x55c7b026aa20 base=0x55c7b49c15d0
CALL _connect_to_scene_recursive: current=0x55c7b52fa310 base=0x55c7b49c15d0
CALL _connect_to_scene_recursive: current=0x55c7b52fa310 base=0x55c7b49c15d0
CALL _connect_to_scene_recursive: current=0x55c7b4c570c0 base=0x55c7b49c15d0
CALL _connect_to_scene_recursive: current=0x55c7b4c570c0 base=0x55c7b49c15d0

This appears to be the normal load of a scene when not upgrading but this double load is the cause of the crash.

Inside of _connect_to_scene_recursive

There is a call below
p_current->connect(SNAME("child_entered_tree"), callable_mp(this, &ScriptEditor::_connect_to_scene_recursive).bind(p_base), CONNECT_DEFERRED);

There is a chance, that when the above message is processed (due to a delay of some sort)., the Node has already been freed,
due to the double processing of the tree. This scenario is when i see a nullptr get passed into _connect_to_scene_recursive since
the node no longer exists.

Two possible solution for this scenario I found, neither might be correct though.
- Add nullptr check to top of _connect_to_scene_recursive. (Add a warning if this scenario is hit).
- Remove the CONNECT_DEFERRED from the call above.

Hope this make sense.
